title: United States Senate Youth Program
costNote: All expenses paid plus a college scholarship
description: Two students from each state who serve in an elected or appointed student leadership office spend a week in Washington meeting senators, cabinet officials, and Supreme Court justices, and receive a college scholarship.

title: U.S. Senate Page Program
costNote: Paid position; housing provided for a fee
description: High school juniors who are at least 16 serve as pages on the Senate floor, attend the Senate Page School, and see the legislative process up close. Appointments are made by sponsoring senators.

title: The Congressional Award
costNote: One-time registration fee; waivers available
description: Congress's award for young Americans ages 14-24. Participants set and achieve goals in volunteer service, personal development, physical fitness, and expedition to earn certificates and medals.

title: American Legion Boys State
costNote: Usually sponsored by local Legion posts
description: Week-long program where rising seniors build a mock state government, run for office, and pass legislation. Two delegates from each state go on to Boys Nation in Washington, DC.

title: American Legion Auxiliary Girls State
costNote: Usually sponsored by local Auxiliary units
description: Week-long leadership program where rising seniors learn how government works by running for office and governing a mock state. Two delegates per state go on to Girls Nation.

title: YMCA Youth & Government
costNote: Program fees vary by state; scholarships often available
description: Students serve as legislators, lobbyists, attorneys, judges, and journalists in a model state government, culminating in a session at the state capitol.

title: Close Up Washington Programs
costNote: Program fee with need-based fellowships
description: Week-long civic education trips to Washington, DC, where students meet with members of Congress, debate policy issues, and study government at monuments and memorials.

title: Junior State of America (JSA)
costNote: Chapter dues; summer schools charge tuition with aid
description: Student-run organization for political debate and civic engagement, with chapter conventions and summer schools at universities focused on government and leadership.

title: National Speech & Debate Association
costNote: Membership through your school team
description: The national honor society and league for speech and debate, with events like policy, Lincoln-Douglas, public forum, congressional debate, and original oratory.

title: Model United Nations
costNote: Conference fees vary
description: Students represent countries in simulated UN committees, researching global issues, negotiating, and drafting resolutions at conferences hosted by schools and universities.

title: National History Day
costNote: Small contest fees vary by state
description: Year-long research program where students create papers, exhibits, documentaries, performances, or websites on a historical topic tied to an annual theme.

title: We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution
costNote: Offered through participating teachers
description: Classes study the Constitution and Bill of Rights, then compete in simulated congressional hearings in front of judges, advancing from state to national finals.

title: National High School Mock Trial Championship
organization: National High School Mock Trial Championship
costNote: Fees vary by state program
description: Teams act as attorneys and witnesses in a simulated trial judged by real attorneys and judges, advancing from state championships to the national championship.

title: National High School Ethics Bowl
organization: Parr Center for Ethics, UNC Chapel Hill
costNote: Usually free for teams
description: A collaborative discussion competition where teams analyze real ethical dilemmas and are judged on the quality of their reasoning, not on beating opponents.

title: C-SPAN StudentCam
costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes
description: National video documentary competition for students in grades 6-12. Students create short documentaries on a yearly civics theme for cash prizes and a chance to air on C-SPAN.

title: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
organization: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
costNote: Free to enter; cash awards for winners
description: Students write an essay about an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official since 1917. Winners receive cash awards and are honored at the Kennedy Library.

title: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
costNote: Free, including tuition, housing, and travel
description: Free six-week college-level seminar in the humanities and social sciences focused on critical Black studies and anti-oppressive studies, with no grades or credit, just learning.

title: HOBY State Leadership Seminars
costNote: Fees are often covered by schools or sponsors
description: Multi-day leadership seminars for high school sophomores focused on personal leadership, group collaboration, and community service, followed by a service commitment.

title: Running Start Young Women's Political Leadership Program
costNote: Free, with travel and lodging covered
description: Week-long program in Washington, DC that introduces high school young women to political leadership through workshops with elected officials and campaign experts.

title: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
costNote: Merit-based scholarship covering travel, tuition, and homestay
description: Full scholarships for students ages 15-18 to learn critical languages such as Arabic, Chinese, Korean, Russian, or Turkish through summer or academic-year programs abroad.

title: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX)
costNote: Full scholarship for a year in Germany
description: Scholarship for students ages 15-18.5 to spend an academic year in Germany living with a host family and attending a German high school.

title: Kennedy-Lugar YES Abroad
costNote: Full scholarship for an academic year abroad
description: Merit-based scholarships for U.S. students ages 15-18.5 to spend an academic year in countries with significant Muslim populations, living with a host family.

title: U.S. Presidential Scholars Program
costNote: Honor by invitation only; students cannot apply on their own
description: One of the nation's highest honors for graduating high school seniors, recognizing academic, artistic, and career and technical achievement.

title: West Point Summer Leaders Experience
costNote: Program fee with financial assistance available
description: Week-long program for high school juniors to experience academics, military training, and athletics at West Point.

title: U.S. Naval Academy Summer Seminar
costNote: Program fee with financial assistance available
description: Week-long program for rising seniors to experience life as a midshipman, with academic workshops, leadership training, and physical fitness.

title: American Legion Oratorical Contest
costNote: Free to enter; college scholarships for winners
description: Students deliver a prepared speech on the U.S. Constitution and an assigned topic, competing from local and state levels to national finals for college scholarships.

title: Educators Rising
costNote: Membership through your school chapter
description: Career organization for high school students interested in becoming teachers, with hands-on teaching experience, competitions, and a national conference.

title: Student Poll Worker Programs
organization: U.S. Election Assistance Commission & local election offices
costNote: Poll workers are usually paid; many states accept workers ages 16-17
description: Many states allow high school students to serve as paid poll workers on Election Day, helping voters and seeing democracy in action. Rules vary by state.
